newsitem.title: GERMANY: German 2.5 pct 97 growth f'cast "very bold"-BGA.
newsitem.headline: German 2.5 pct 97 growth f'cast "very bold"-BGA.

text.p: The head of Germany's Wholesale and Foreign Trade Federation (BGA) said on Friday that a forecast of 2.5 percent growth in 1997 by a panel of independent government economic advisors was optimistic.
BGA president Michael Fuchs told reporters the forecast by the so-called five wise men was "very bold".
Finance Minister Theo Waigel has used the forecast as a basis for drafting his 1997 budget -- intended to cut borrowing enough for Germany to qualify for European monetary union.
Despite predicting stronger growth, the panel still expected unemployment to rise to a post-unification high of over four million next year, Fuchs noted.

Fuchs said more should be done to cut the tax and welfare overheads burdening employers in the underdeveloped German services sector -- which has created 1.6 million jobs since 1989 while over 800,000 jobs have been lost in industry.
